title: Compatible inverse image of profinite coefficient sheaves
statement:
Let $u:U\to V$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-etale sites and their universe convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and inverse image $u^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $(Q_n,t_n:Q_{n+1}\to Q_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a countable inverse system of finite commutative rings with unital ring maps, all in the chosen universe. For $T=U,V$, let $(Q_n)_T$ be the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], equivalently the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $W\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|W|),Q_n)$ with $Q_n$ discrete, and put $R_T=\varprojlim_n(Q_n)_T$, with projections $\pi_{T,n}:R_T\to(Q_n)_T$. There are canonical isomorphisms of sheaves of rings
$$
 c_{u,n}:u^{-1}(Q_n)_V\xrightarrow{\sim}(Q_n)_U,\qquad
 c_u:u^{-1}R_V\xrightarrow{\sim}R_U.
$$
Here $c_{u,n}$ is adjoint to the map $(Q_n)_V\to u_*(Q_n)_U$ sending each constant section $q$ to the same constant section $q$ on the base-changed object. The map $c_u$ is the unique map whose $n$-th projection is $c_{u,n}\circ u^{-1}\pi_{V,n}$; this canonical comparison is an isomorphism, not merely a map to a limit. These identifications satisfy
$$
 \pi_{U,n}\circ c_u=c_{u,n}\circ u^{-1}\pi_{V,n},\qquad
 (t_n)_U\circ c_{u,n+1}=c_{u,n}\circ u^{-1}(t_n)_V.
$$
They are natural in morphisms of inverse systems of finite rings and compatible with identities and composition of scheme morphisms, under the canonical identifications of composite inverse images.

proof.text: For a scheme $Z$ over $T$, write $h_Z(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_T(W,Z)$ on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$. This is a sheaf: a pro-etale covering is fpqc, so compatible morphisms glue uniquely by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. The glued morphism is over $T$, since its two composites to $T$ agree on the cover and uniqueness of descent into $T$ makes them agree globally. Thus the small pro-etale site is subcanonical, including for every object that will be constructed below.

For a finite ring $Q$, use [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] to form the scheme $E_{T,Q}=\coprod_{q\in Q}T$, with ring-object operations given on labels by the operations of $Q$. A map $W\to E_{T,Q}$ over $T$ is precisely a partition $W=\coprod_{q\in Q}W_q$ into open-and-closed subschemes: on $W_q$ it is the structure morphism to the copy labelled $q$. Consequently $h_{E_{T,Q}}$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf $Q$, as follows directly from the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Given any map from that presheaf to a sheaf $F$, send a partition to the section obtained by gluing the image of the constant section $q$ over each $W_q$. These opens form a pro-etale cover: each is an open immersion with identity maps on local rings and hence flat with flat diagonal, and they have a finite affine refinement on every affine open: refine their intersections with $\operatorname{Spec}B$ by basic opens $D(f)$; these cover the spectrum, so their $f$ generate the unit ideal (otherwise a maximal ideal containing them would give an uncovered point); writing $1$ as a finite linear combination gives a finite subcover. Uniqueness of sheaf gluing shows that this extension is unique and natural in $W$. For a ring-valued $F$ the extension is a ring map: on the common refinement $W_q\cap W'_{q'}$ the sum and product are respectively the images of $q+q'$ and $qq'$. Thus $(Q)_T=h_{E_{T,Q}}$ canonically as ring sheaves. The constant $q$ is the map to the labelled copy. A ring map $Q\to Q'$ acts by the same label map on these schemes. The partition description also gives the stated continuous-functions description: a map to finite discrete $Q$ is continuous exactly when its fibres are clopen, and it factors uniquely through the quotient space of connected components.

proof.text: Put $E_{T,n}=E_{T,Q_n}$ with transition sending the copy labelled $q$ to that labelled $t_n(q)$. Each transition is affine: over an affine open in one target copy its inverse image is a finite disjoint union of that affine open, with coordinate ring a finite product of its ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] to this countable directed system to obtain $E_T=\varprojlim_n E_{T,n}$. Over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset T$, the restriction is $\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_n B^{Q_n})$. Indeed the limit theorem permits restriction to the open $\coprod_{Q_1}\operatorname{Spec}B$ in $E_{T,1}$, and its affine-limit clause gives this formula. Every $B^{Q_n}$ is an etale algebra of finite presentation over $B$: its spectrum is finitely many copies of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, and on each copy the map is the identity (flat, with open diagonal and finite presentation). Hence the displayed colimit is ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], and is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. Weak etaleness is the condition of flatness on the local ring maps and on those of the diagonal; the affine restrictions cover both source and diagonal, so $E_T\to T$ is weakly etale. The same applies to $E_{T,n}\to T$. All these schemes belong to the chosen universe: a countable colimit of rings and a finite product stay in the universe, and the affine descriptions glue over the small set of affine opens of $T$. Thus they are objects of the specified small pro-etale site.

proof.text: For every $W\to T$, the scheme-limit universal property gives $\operatorname{Mor}_T(W,E_T)=\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Mor}_T(W,E_{T,n})$, with the indicated projections. By Step 2 and the sectionwise computation of ring-sheaf limits [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], this identifies $h_{E_T}$ with the underlying sheaf of $R_T$. Endow $E_T$ with its ring-object operations by the limit universal property: for example the $n$-th component of addition is addition in $E_{T,n}$ after the two projections, and zero and one are the compatible labelled sections. The ring axioms hold after every projection and therefore hold by uniqueness. Under the displayed sectionwise identification, these are exactly the componentwise ring operations of $R_T$, and $h_{E_T}\to h_{E_{T,n}}$ is exactly $\pi_{T,n}$.

Let $b_u:V_{\mathrm{proet}}\to U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ be base change. For any object $Z\to V$, Step 1 and [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection], applied to the two small site categories, give for every sheaf of sets $F$ on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(u^{-1}h_Z,F)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_Z,u_*F)=(u_*F)(Z)=F(U\times_V Z)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_{U\times_V Z},F)$. Here the first and third equalities are the adjunction and the direct-image evaluation formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The uniqueness result [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] gives $u^{-1}h_Z\cong h_{U\times_V Z}$. It is natural in $Z$ because every displayed bijection is natural in the representing object as well as in $F$. Its adjoint is the map $h_Z\to u_*h_{U\times_V Z}$ sending $W\to Z$ to its base change $U\times_V W\to U\times_V Z$, as is seen by evaluation on the identity of $Z$.

proof.text: Base change identifies $U\times_V E_{V,n}$ with $E_{U,n}$ by preserving labels. It also identifies $U\times_V E_V$ with $E_U$: for an arbitrary $U$-scheme $W$, a map $W\to U\times_V E_V$ over $U$ is a $V$-map $W\to E_V$, hence a compatible family of $V$-maps $W\to E_{V,n}$, hence a compatible family of $U$-maps $W\to U\times_V E_{V,n}$. This is exactly the limit universal property defining $E_U$. The unique isomorphism is therefore compatible with all projections and with the label maps of the tower. Apply Step 5 to $Z=E_{V,n}$ and $Z=E_V$, and then Steps 2 and 4. This produces isomorphisms of underlying sheaves $c_{u,n}$ and $c_u$, compatible with the transitions and all projections. In particular it proves that this specific infinite-limit comparison is invertible, without asserting preservation of arbitrary infinite limits by $u^{-1}$.

proof.text: These underlying-sheaf isomorphisms are ring isomorphisms, with the inverse-image ring structures meant in the statement. To justify this compatibility, [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-sets-left-exact] applies to $b_u$, since it preserves the final object and fibre products by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; composing with the finite-limit-preserving sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] shows that the set-valued $u^{-1}$ preserves finite products. It therefore sends a ring object to a ring object by applying it to addition, multiplication, zero, one and negation, using the canonical product identifications. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects] this gives a sheaf of rings. The set adjunction restricts to the ring adjunction: naturality of its unit and counit, together with their finite-product identifications, makes the equations for commuting with each operation equivalent for adjoint maps. This characterizes the ring inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For a representable ring object, Step 5 is compatible with products: evaluate the Hom bijection at a pair of sections and its two projections; the result is their pair after base change. Naturality in each scheme-operation map then proves compatibility with all five ring operations. The base-change identifications of Step 6 preserve these operations too, since at each finite coordinate they preserve labels. Finally, the adjunct of $c_{u,n}$ sends the constant $q$ to the same labelled constant $q$ on a base-changed object, so it is precisely the specified adjunct, not a different isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 00WJ and 04D3, labels lemma-sheafification-exact and lemma-pullback-representable-sheaf; ring-object interpretation

proof.text: By the projection compatibility in Step 6, $\pi_{U,n}\circ c_u=c_{u,n}\circ u^{-1}\pi_{V,n}$. The same naturality applied to the label map $t_n$ gives $(t_n)_U\circ c_{u,n+1}=c_{u,n}\circ u^{-1}(t_n)_V$. The limit universal property says that the first equations uniquely determine $c_u$. A morphism of towers induces the corresponding label maps at every level and the unique map between their representing limits; naturality of Step 5 proves the desired naturality, with its infinite-level square checked after each projection. For $u=\mathrm{id}$ the adjoint map is the identity label map; the resulting comparison is the identity. For $U\xrightarrow{u}V\xrightarrow{v}T$, base-changing a map twice and once along $v\circ u$ gives the same map under the fibre-product association isomorphism. The adjunct descriptions in Step 5 therefore identify the finite-level comparisons with $c_{u,n}\circ u^{-1}c_{v,n}$ under the canonical composite-inverse-image identification. Checking after each projection gives the identical composition law for $c_u$. This proves all clauses, including identity and composition coherence.
